question: Estimate Punctual Pros revenue from public filings
html:
Punctual Pros Revenue Estimate

Public filings put Punctual Pros' FY2025 pro forma revenue at ~$22M est. (range $16-28M): ~$18M from Pennsylvania and ~$3-5M from the New Jersey add-on (Punctual Pros public filings). Confidence is medium. No filing discloses revenue directly.

How the estimate is built

  • PPP payroll anchor. The Rohrer Company's April 2020 PPP loan of $745,985 implies ~$3.58M of 2019 payroll (high confidence). That supports ~50-58 employees and ~$9-12M of 2019 revenue est. (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Headcount scaling. ~113 employees by 2024 at ~$76K Lancaster wages and a 40-45% labor ratio gives a PA run-rate of ~$18-22M est. at the Apr 3, 2024 entry. The firm profile flags the 113 figure as not re-verified (BSP firm profile).
  • Franchise disclosure cross-check. The 2026 franchise disclosure document lists 25 territories operated: 19 PA and 6 NJ. Mapping these to Item 19 quartiles gives ~$12-19M PA and ~$3-5M NJ est. for FY2025 (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Add-on. Horvath Home Services' PPP loan of $251,894 implies ~$1.21M payroll and ~$3-4M of 2019 revenue est.
MetricEstimateConfidence
2019 Rohrer revenue~$9-12M est.Low
FY2025 PA revenue~$18M est. ($12-24M)Medium
FY2025 pro forma total~$22M est. ($16-28M)Medium
Revenue per territory~$0.9M est.Low
Adjusted EBITDA~$2.6M est. ($1.8-3.1M)Low

What the numbers imply

  • Revenue per territory of ~$0.9M est. sits above system averages of $0.61M (One Hour) and $0.66M (Ben Franklin). This is either real outperformance or an overstated blend.
  • Royalty plus brand fund takes ~7.2-7.5% of revenue (~$1.6M a year est.). That caps adjusted EBITDA margins at about 8-14% est.
  • PGIM Private Credit Fund's Jun 30, 2026 10-Q shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco at 8.73%, maturing Mar 26, 2029. Funded amount is $4.83M at ~98.6% of par, plus $1.4M unfunded. That is modest against ~$2.6M EBITDA est.

Caveats

  • The source set was checked on Sep 24, 2026. Of 30 items sampled, 29 were confirmed and 1 was removed (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • The labor-ratio assumption (30-45% of revenue) drives most of the range.
  • The territory mapping assumes quartile placement. It does not use actual unit sales.
  • Actual FY2025 revenue would come from the management accounts or the lender compliance package. Those figures should replace this estimate.

Next actions

  1. Reconcile the ~$22M est. against FY2025 audited or management financials. Record the variance by method.
  2. Pull territory-level revenue from royalty reports. Check whether the ~$0.9M per territory holds or is driven by a few One Hour units.
  3. Confirm current headcount and labor cost. This refreshes the payroll-based method.
  4. Model margin sensitivity to the ~7.2-7.5% franchise fee load against the 2026 growth plan.

# Punctual Pros Revenue Estimate

Public filings put Punctual Pros' FY2025 pro forma revenue at **~$22M est. (range $16-28M)**: ~$18M from Pennsylvania and ~$3-5M from the New Jersey add-on (Punctual Pros public filings). Confidence is medium. No filing discloses revenue directly.

## How the estimate is built

- **PPP payroll anchor.** The Rohrer Company's April 2020 PPP loan of $745,985 implies ~$3.58M of 2019 payroll (high confidence). That supports ~50-58 employees and ~$9-12M of 2019 revenue est. (Punctual Pros public filings).
- **Headcount scaling.** ~113 employees by 2024 at ~$76K Lancaster wages and a 40-45% labor ratio gives a PA run-rate of ~$18-22M est. at the Apr 3, 2024 entry. The firm profile flags the 113 figure as not re-verified (BSP firm profile).
- **Franchise disclosure cross-check.** The 2026 franchise disclosure document lists 25 territories operated: 19 PA and 6 NJ. Mapping these to Item 19 quartiles gives ~$12-19M PA and ~$3-5M NJ est. for FY2025 (Punctual Pros public filings).
- **Add-on.** Horvath Home Services' PPP loan of $251,894 implies ~$1.21M payroll and ~$3-4M of 2019 revenue est.

| Metric | Estimate | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| 2019 Rohrer revenue | ~$9-12M est. | Low |
| FY2025 PA revenue | ~$18M est. ($12-24M) | Medium |
| FY2025 pro forma total | ~$22M est. ($16-28M) | Medium |
| Revenue per territory | ~$0.9M est. | Low |
| Adjusted EBITDA | ~$2.6M est. ($1.8-3.1M) | Low |

## What the numbers imply

- Revenue per territory of ~$0.9M est. sits above system averages of $0.61M (One Hour) and $0.66M (Ben Franklin). This is either real outperformance or an overstated blend.
- Royalty plus brand fund takes ~7.2-7.5% of revenue (~$1.6M a year est.). That caps adjusted EBITDA margins at about 8-14% est.
- PGIM Private Credit Fund's Jun 30, 2026 10-Q shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco at 8.73%, maturing Mar 26, 2029. Funded amount is $4.83M at ~98.6% of par, plus $1.4M unfunded. That is modest against ~$2.6M EBITDA est.

## Caveats

- The source set was checked on Sep 24, 2026. Of 30 items sampled, 29 were confirmed and 1 was removed (Punctual Pros public filings).
- The labor-ratio assumption (30-45% of revenue) drives most of the range.
- The territory mapping assumes quartile placement. It does not use actual unit sales.
- Actual FY2025 revenue would come from the management accounts or the lender compliance package. Those figures should replace this estimate.

## Next actions

1. Reconcile the ~$22M est. against FY2025 audited or management financials. Record the variance by method.
2. Pull territory-level revenue from royalty reports. Check whether the ~$0.9M per territory holds or is driven by a few One Hour units.
3. Confirm current headcount and labor cost. This refreshes the payroll-based method.
4. Model margin sensitivity to the ~7.2-7.5% franchise fee load against the 2026 growth plan.
